# Napkin script: every verb

<!-- Generated by `npm run api-docs` from src/core/script/verbs.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Napkin script 1: 56 verbs in 10 categories, each with every way of writing it, what it does, and an example that runs as written. In a form, `<width>` is a value to give, `[r <radius>]` may be left out, and `px|in|mm|pt` is one word of those.

## Document

The page: its size, background and name, the unit bare numbers are read in, the seed, and more pages.

### `napkin`

```text
napkin <version>
```

The language version the script was written for. The first line of a script; without it version 1 is assumed, with a warning.

```napkin
napkin 1
```

### `page`

```text
page <paper> [portrait|landscape]
page <width> <height> [portrait|landscape]
```

The page size: a named size (a3, a4, a5, letter, legal, tabloid, square, slide, napkin) or a width and a height, turned portrait or landscape.

```napkin
page a4 landscape
```

### `background`

```text
background <color>
background none
```

The page color, or none for a transparent page.

```napkin
background #fcfaf5
```

### `name`

```text
name "<name>"
```

The page's name, and the file stem it is written under.

```napkin
name "Acme Corp card"
```

### `units`

```text
units px|in|mm|pt
```

The unit bare numbers are read in from here on: px, in, mm or pt. Pixels until changed.

```napkin
units mm
```

### `seed`

```text
seed <n>
```

The seed for the hand-drawn pass. One script and one seed draw the same bytes every run.

```napkin
seed 7
```

### `newpage`

```text
newpage ["<name>"]
```

Starts another page the same size, carrying the paint state across.

```napkin
newpage "Back"
```

## Layers

Named layers and nested groups, with opacity, visibility and lock.

### `layer`

```text
layer "<name>" [opacity <0-1>] [hidden] [locked]
```

A drawing layer. Marks after it go on it until the next layer.

```napkin
layer "Sky" opacity 0.8
```

### `group`

```text
group "<name>" [opacity <0-1>] [hidden] [locked] { ... }
```

A group layer. The layer and group lines in its block become its children.

```napkin
group "Figure" {
  layer "Head"
  circle 200 80 30
  layer "Body"
  rect 170 115 60 100
}
```

## Paint

What every mark after it is drawn with: tool, color, width, opacity, fill, gradient, outline, dash, profile, nib, font, and the hand-drawn pass.

### `tool`

```text
tool pen|marker|copic|eraser
```

The kind of mark: pen, marker (translucent, so overlapping passes build up like ink), copic (a broad, angled nib) or eraser (takes away what is under it, on its own layer only).

```napkin
tool marker
```

### `color`

```text
color <color>
```

The ink color of every mark after it.

```napkin
color #1f2328
```

### `width`

```text
width <length>
```

The stroke width of every mark after it.

```napkin
width 3
```

### `opacity`

```text
opacity <0-1>
```

The opacity of every mark after it, from 0 to 1.

```napkin
opacity 0.5
```

### `fill`

```text
fill <color>
fill none
```

The fill color of closed shapes after it, or none.

```napkin
fill #ffe08a
```

### `gradient`

```text
gradient linear <angle> (<color> <offset>, ...)
gradient radial (<color> <offset>, ...)
gradient none
```

A gradient fill for closed shapes after it: linear at an angle, or radial from the centre out, or none.

```napkin
gradient linear 90 (#ffe08a 0, #ff8a65 1)
```

### `stroke`

```text
stroke on|off
```

Turns the outline on or off. With it off, a closed shape is its fill alone.

```napkin
stroke off
```

### `style`

```text
style solid|dashed|dotted
```

The outline's dash: solid, dashed or dotted.

```napkin
style dashed
```

### `profile`

```text
profile uniform|rounded|tapered|wave
```

How the width runs along a pen or marker stroke: uniform, rounded, tapered or wave.

```napkin
profile tapered
```

### `nib`

```text
nib <degrees>
```

The angle of the copic nib, in degrees.

```napkin
nib 30
```

### `rough`

```text
rough <0-1> [passes 1|2] [overshoot <length>]
rough off
```

The hand-drawn pass for every mark after it: 0 is exact, 1 is clearly drawn by hand, and off is 0. Seeded, so it draws the same way every run.

```napkin
rough 0.6 passes 2
```

### `font`

```text
font "<family>" [<size>]
font <size>
```

The font family and size of text after it.

```napkin
font "Georgia" 24
```

## Shapes

Marks built from Bezier anchors: rectangles, circles, ellipses, lines, polygons, stars, arcs, spirals and the shape library.

### `rect`

```text
rect <x> <y> <width> <height> [r <radius>]
```

A rectangle, with rounded corners when r is given.

```napkin
rect 20 20 360 80 r 12
```

### `circle`

```text
circle <cx> <cy> <r>
```

A circle, drawn as four cubic curves rather than a polygon.

```napkin
circle 50% 50% 48
```

### `ellipse`

```text
ellipse <cx> <cy> <rx> <ry>
```

An ellipse, from its centre and two radii.

```napkin
ellipse 200 150 120 60
```

### `line`

```text
line <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2>
```

A straight line between two points.

```napkin
line 20 20 380 280
```

### `polygon`

```text
polygon <x> <y>, <x> <y>, ... [r <radius>]
```

A closed shape through a list of points, with rounded corners when r is given.

```napkin
polygon 200 40, 360 260, 40 260 r 8
```

### `polyline`

```text
polyline <x> <y>, <x> <y>, ...
```

An open line through a list of points.

```napkin
polyline 20 200, 120 120, 220 200, 320 120
```

### `star`

```text
star <cx> <cy> <outer> <inner> <count>
```

A star with the given number of points, between an outer and an inner radius.

```napkin
star 200 150 80 32 5
```

### `arc`

```text
arc <cx> <cy> <r> <from> <to>
```

An open arc of a circle between two angles, in degrees clockwise from three o'clock.

```napkin
arc 200 150 80 0 90
```

### `spiral`

```text
spiral <cx> <cy> <r> <turns>
```

A spiral winding out from its centre to the radius over the given number of turns.

```napkin
spiral 200 150 90 3
```

### `shape`

```text
shape "<name>" at <x> <y> size <width> [<height>]
```

A named shape from the built-in library, drawn in a box from x, y. With one size its longer side is that long and it keeps its proportions; with a width and a height it is stretched to fill them.

```napkin
shape "cube-isometric" at 40 40 size 120
```

## Paths

Marks written segment by segment, from SVG path data or from a block of steps, and curves through points.

### `path`

```text
path "<svg path data>"
path { ... }
```

One mark, from SVG path data or from a block of path steps. Each subpath of a compound path is one piece of the same mark.

```napkin
path "M20 20 C60 0 100 40 140 20"
```

### `move`

```text
move <x> <y>
```

Starts a new subpath at a point.

```napkin
path {
  move 20 20
  to 120 20
  move 20 60
  to 120 60
}
```

### `to`

```text
to <x> <y>
```

A straight segment to a point.

```napkin
path {
  move 20 20
  to 120 20
  to 120 80
}
```

### `by`

```text
by <dx> <dy>
```

A straight segment by an offset from the current point.

```napkin
path {
  move 20 20
  by 100 0
  by 0 60
  close
}
```

### `curve`

```text
curve <c1x> <c1y> <c2x> <c2y> <x> <y>
```

A cubic curve to a point, steered by two handles.

```napkin
path {
  move 20 100
  curve 60 20 140 20 180 100
}
```

### `smooth`

```text
smooth <c2x> <c2y> <x> <y>
```

A cubic curve whose first handle mirrors the last one, so the join stays smooth.

```napkin
path {
  move 20 100
  curve 60 20 140 20 180 100
  smooth 300 180 340 100
}
```

### `through`

```text
through <x> <y>, <x> <y>, ...
```

A smooth curve through a list of points. Inside a path block it continues the subpath; outside one it is an open mark of its own.

```napkin
through 20 100, 80 40, 140 100, 200 40, 260 100
```

### `close`

```text
close
```

Closes the current subpath back to its start.

```napkin
path {
  move 20 20
  to 120 20
  to 70 100
  close
}
```

## Transforms

Translate, rotate, scale and mirror, baked into the anchors of every mark after them, with push and pop to undo them.

### `push`

```text
push
```

Saves the transform, the paint state and the units, for the next pop to restore.

```napkin
push
rotate 15 at 200 150
rect 150 100 100 100
pop
```

### `pop`

```text
pop
```

Restores the transform, the paint state and the units the last push saved.

```napkin
push
translate 40 0
circle 100 100 20
pop
```

### `translate`

```text
translate <dx> <dy>
```

Moves everything drawn after it.

```napkin
translate 40 0
```

### `rotate`

```text
rotate <degrees> [at <x> <y>]
```

Turns everything drawn after it, clockwise in degrees, about the origin or a point given with at.

```napkin
rotate 45 at 200 150
```

### `scale`

```text
scale <s> [<sy>] [at <x> <y>]
```

Scales everything drawn after it, about the origin or a point given with at. One factor scales both ways.

```napkin
scale 2 at 200 150
```

### `mirror`

```text
mirror x|y [at <position>]
```

Reflects everything drawn after it: x swaps left and right across a vertical line, y swaps top and bottom across a horizontal one, at 0 unless given.

```napkin
mirror x at 200
```

## Control

Named numbers, reusable definitions, and repetition.

### `let`

```text
let <name> <value>
```

Names a number for the expressions after it, in the current units.

```napkin
let gap 24
rect 20 20 (gap * 4) (gap * 2)
```

### `define`

```text
define "<name>" { ... }
```

Records a block of drawing under a name without drawing it, for place to draw.

```napkin
define "tick" {
  line 0 10 4 14
  line 4 14 14 0
}
place "tick" at 40 40 scale 2
```

### `place`

```text
place "<name>" [at <x> <y>] [scale <s>] [rotate <degrees>]
```

Draws a definition, moved, scaled or turned.

```napkin
define "tick" {
  line 0 10 4 14
  line 4 14 14 0
}
place "tick" at 40 40 scale 2 rotate 15
```

### `repeat`

```text
repeat <count> [as <name>] { ... }
```

Runs a block a number of times, counting from 0 in the name given with as.

```napkin
repeat 10 as i {
  rect (20 + i * 36) 20 30 30
}
```

## Text and media

Text, placed images, linked files, and documents the host supplied.

### `text`

```text
text "<text>" at <x> <y> [size <size>] [box <width>] [align left|center|right] [as marks]
```

A text item, measured and aligned, and editable in the app. With as marks the letters are drawn as pen strokes instead.

```napkin
text "Acme Corp" at 200 70 size 28 align center
```

### `image`

```text
image "<asset or data URL>" at <x> <y> [size <width> [<height>]]
```

Places an image: an asset the host supplied, by name, or a data URL. Nothing is read from disk.

```napkin
image "logo" at 20 20 size 120
```

### `link`

```text
link "<path>" at <x> <y> [size <width> [<height>]] [name "<layer name>"]
```

Places a linked file: one selectable element that references the file instead of drawing its contents into the page.

```napkin
link "assets/logo.svg" at 20 120 size 120 120 name "Logo"
```

### `use`

```text
use "<document>" [at <x> <y>] [scale <s>] [layer "<name>"]
```

Copies in a document the host supplied, as a group, with its layers and anchors.

```napkin
use "badge" at 200 40 scale 0.5
```

## Effects

Blur, shadow and color effects for the next layer, group or mark, as CSS filter functions are: drawn in SVG, in PNG and in the app, and left out of a PDF.

### `effect`

```text
effect blur <radius>
effect brightness <amount>
effect contrast <amount>
effect saturate <amount>
effect grayscale [<0-1>]
effect sepia [<0-1>]
effect invert [<0-1>]
effect hue-rotate <degrees>
effect opacity <0-1>
effect drop-shadow <dx> <dy> <blur> <color>
effect none
```

An effect for the next layer, group or mark the script makes, as its CSS filter function works: blur, brightness, contrast, saturate, grayscale, sepia, invert, hue-rotate, opacity or drop-shadow. Several stack in order, and none clears what is waiting.

```napkin
effect drop-shadow 4 4 8 #00000066
rect 40 40 200 120 r 12
```

## Output

Hints the renderers read: the box every output is cut to, and one box every page shares.

### `crop`

```text
crop auto [pad <length>]
crop none
crop <x> <y> <width> <height>
```

The box every output is cut to: auto fits the ink with room to spare, none keeps the page, or a box given outright.

```napkin
crop auto pad 12
```

### `registration`

```text
registration <x> <y> <width> <height>
```

One box every page is written in, so frames drawn by one script line up when they are played in sequence.

```napkin
registration 0 0 400 300
```

## Library shapes

`shape "<name>" at <x> <y> size <width>` draws one of these: `square`, `rectangle`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `triangle`, `right-triangle`, `hexagon`, `star`, `horizontal`, `vertical`, `45-degree`, `15-degree`, `arc`, `spiral`, `wheel-isometric`, `sphere-isometric`, `cube-isometric`, `cylinder-isometric`, `wheel-perspective`, `sphere-perspective`, `cube-perspective`, `cylinder-perspective`.

## Functions

An expression in parentheses can call these:

| Function | Takes | Gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sin` | a number | The sine of an angle in degrees. |
| `cos` | a number | The cosine of an angle in degrees. |
| `tan` | a number | The tangent of an angle in degrees. |
| `sqrt` | a number | The square root. |
| `abs` | a number | The value without its sign. |
| `round` | a number | The nearest whole number. |
| `floor` | a number | The whole number at or below. |
| `ceil` | a number | The whole number at or above. |
| `min` | 2 or more numbers | The smallest of two or more values. |
| `max` | 2 or more numbers | The largest of two or more values. |

## Diagnostic codes

| Code | Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unknown-verb` | error | A line starts with a word that is not a verb. |
| `misplaced-verb` | error | A verb where it cannot appear: a path step outside a path block, a napkin line after the first, a layer inside a path, a newpage inside a group or a definition. |
| `unsupported-verb` | error | The verb, or this way of writing it, is known but not drawn by this build or by the host running the script; the instruction is skipped. |
| `expected-number` | error | A number, or an expression in parentheses, was expected. |
| `expected-length` | error | A length was expected: a number, a number with a unit (10mm, 0.5in, 12pt, 4px), a percentage, or an expression. |
| `expected-string` | error | A double-quoted string was expected. |
| `expected-identifier` | error | A bare name was expected: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. |
| `expected-color` | error | A CSS color was expected, such as #1f2328, red or rgb(31, 35, 40). |
| `expected-choice` | error | One word from a fixed list was expected; the message lists them. |
| `expected-points` | error | A list of points was expected: x y pairs separated by commas. |
| `expected-stops` | error | A list of gradient stops was expected: (color offset, color offset, ...). |
| `unexpected-token` | error | Something is left on the line after the instruction was read, or a character that cannot start anything. |
| `missing-argument` | error | A required argument is missing; the message names it and shows how the verb is written. |
| `expected-block` | error | A block was expected: { at the end of the line, the instructions it holds, and } to close it. |
| `unclosed-block` | error | A block opened with { is never closed with }. |
| `unexpected-close` | error | A } closes a block that was never opened. |
| `unclosed-string` | error | A string runs to the end of the line without its closing quote. |
| `invalid-expression` | error | An expression could not be read: an unknown operator, a missing operand, or an unclosed parenthesis. |
| `unit-unknown` | error | A number carries a unit the language does not know. The units are px, in, mm and pt, and % for a share of the page. |
| `invalid-value` | error | A value is out of range: an opacity above 1, a negative radius, a star with fewer than 2 points, a percentage where the page cannot measure one. |
| `version-missing` | warning | The script does not start with napkin <version>; version 1 is assumed. |
| `version-unsupported` | error | The script names a version newer than this build reads; the message names the newest it does. |
| `unknown-variable` | error | An expression uses a name no let or repeat has set. |
| `unknown-definition` | error | place names something no define recorded. |
| `unknown-shape` | error | shape names something the shape library does not have. |
| `unknown-asset` | error | image names an asset the host did not supply. |
| `unknown-document` | error | use names a document the host did not supply. |
| `image-size-unknown` | warning | An image's size cannot be read from its data, so it is placed square: 100 by 100, or the one size given by itself. |
| `glyph-missing` | warning | text as marks has a character the built-in face does not draw; it is left as a gap. |
| `unknown-field` | warning | An instruction in a JSON script has a field its verb does not have; it is left out. |
| `recursive-definition` | error | A definition places itself, directly or through another definition. |
| `division-by-zero` | error | An expression divides by zero. |
| `budget-exceeded` | error | The script ran more instructions, drew more marks, emitted more anchors or sampled points, or nested deeper than the limit allows; what it drew up to that point is kept. |
| `pop-without-push` | error | pop with nothing saved to restore. |
| `unbalanced-push` | warning | A push is never popped before its block ends; the saved state is restored there anyway. |
| `duplicate-definition` | warning | A second define replaces an earlier one of the same name. |
| `link-unresolved` | warning | A linked file could not be read for an output that has to draw it, so its placeholder was drawn instead. |
| `unused-effect` | warning | An effect nothing took: no layer, group or mark followed it before its block, its page or the script ended. |
